key_insight: Budget Muon (BMuon) modifies Muon’s spectral geometry so MLP hidden channels compete for a shared budget, making trained Transformers more robust to structured channel pruning.
engineering_relevance: BMuon offers an interpretable global channel budget and learned pruning scores for reducing Transformer MLP width while preserving more performance than Muon in the reported evaluations.
method: Formulate normalized steepest descent under norms interpolating between Muon’s geometry and structured sparse geometries.
Allocate a shared budget across hidden channels and approximate the exact allocation problem with a minorization–maximization surrogate.
Prove width-minimal minimum-cost representations for linear factorization models under sufficiently scarce BMuon budgets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improvements over Muon for gradual MLP pruning of ViT-S/16 on ImageNet-1K and post-training MLP pruning of a 1B-parameter LLaMA-style model trained on FineWeb; learned allocations also outperform weight-magnitude pruning scores in the vision evaluation.
watch_item: The width-minimality guarantee concerns linear factorization models, while practical Transformer training uses an allocation surrogate whose overhead and approximation effects require evaluation.
paper_title: BMuon: Budgeting Muon's Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility
